title: Your first project
sub: The template, the files and the path to the first window
cards/0/body: You install the templates once, then create a project with a single command.
cards/1/body:
Program.cs: the entry point, sets up Avalonia.
App.axaml: the application and its theme.
App.axaml.cs: creates the main window.
Views/MainWindow.axaml: the window markup.
ViewModels/MainWindowViewModel.cs: the window's data and logic.

The .axaml extension is XAML for Avalonia. It was chosen so IDEs do not confuse it with WPF.
cards/2/body: UsePlatformDetect works out how to open windows on the current system.
cards/3/body: Once the framework is ready, the app creates the main window and hands it a view model.
cards/4/q: Put the startup steps in order
cards/4/explain: Five steps from Main to a window, and you can see each of them in the template code.
cards/5/q: Match each file to its role
cards/6/q: Create a project from the MVVM template
cards/6/explain: dotnet new creates a project from a template.
cards/7/q: Why do markup files use .axaml instead of .xaml?
cards/7/options/0: So IDEs and tools do not mistake them for WPF markup
cards/7/explain: Inside, it is XAML with Avalonia's own namespace.
cards/8/q: Where does the window get its view model?
cards/8/options/2: Avalonia finds it by name on its own
cards/8/explain: DataContext is the key word of the next units: bindings get their data from it.
